_readme: Single source of truth for SOP business rules and capability classification. Adding/adjusting a rule for a new or existing SOP is a change to THIS file, not to rules.py, config.py, hybrid_search.py, or synthesizer.py. Those files load this registry instead of hardcoding KB numbers. See daemon/safety/kb_capabilities.py for how 'capabilityTagsAny' matching and legacy fallback work.

capability_inference._readme: Used only when a KB article has no explicit capabilityTags field (i.e. it hasn't been tagged in the database/JSON dataset yet). Matches on title/category keywords. Once a KB article carries an explicit capabilityTags array, that array is used directly and this inference is skipped for it.

cross_domain_guards._readme: Replaces hardcoded per-file allowlists (config.py LINUX_USER_SOP_NUMBERS, synthesizer.py _db2_allowed_sops). A ticket detected as domain X may only be served a KB carrying one of the listed capability tags.

legacy_kb_number_fallback._readme: Historical KB-number -> capability mapping, preserved only so tickets that already matched a not-yet-tagged KB by number keep the same behavior during migration. Do not add new numbers here; tag the KB article's capabilityTags field instead. Verified against scripts/database/full_platform_data_dump.json on 2026-08-25: several of these numbers now point at unrelated content (KB0000001/14/15/18) because 'number' is an auto-increment field that gets reassigned across dataset reseeds -- kept here only as an inert last-resort match, never as the primary mechanism.

sudoers_sanitizer._readme: Last-resort net for LLM-hallucinated sudoers.d NOPASSWD command specs. The primary fix lives in the SOP-parameterization prompt (daemon/sop/synthesizer.py), which now instructs the model to emit only a literal command path. Do NOT add literal hostnames or ticket-specific words here -- if a new bad token keeps slipping through, that means the prompt instruction needs strengthening, not that this list needs another entry.
